Title: Early symptoms of Alzheimer’s  
Text: Early signs include memory lapses, confusion about time/place, repeating questions, and difficulty performing familiar tasks. If these happen often, please consult a doctor. I can help you track these symptoms.

Title: What increases the risk of Alzheimer’s?  
Text: Risk factors include age, family history, and certain lifestyle conditions like heart disease or diabetes. Having risk factors does not mean someone will surely get Alzheimer’s. It just means being aware and caring for overall health is important.

Title: How is Alzheimer’s diagnosed?  
Text: Doctors usually diagnose Alzheimer’s through memory tests, questions about daily life, physical exams, and sometimes brain scans. There is no single test, but a combination helps rule out other causes. Early check-ups make a big difference.

Title: Is there a cure for Alzheimer’s?  
Text: There is currently no cure for Alzheimer’s. However, treatments and therapies can help manage symptoms and improve quality of life. Support from family, caregivers, and professionals plays a key role in daily care.

Title: How can someone cope with memory loss?  
Text: Simple routines, writing notes, using reminders, and keeping important items in the same place can help. Support from friends and family makes coping easier. Even small acts of patience and kindness make a big difference.

Title: How does Alzheimer’s affect daily life?  
Text: Alzheimer’s can make it harder to remember names, follow conversations, cook, or manage money. Over time, daily activities may need support. Gentle understanding from family and caregivers helps maintain dignity and comfort.

Title: How can families support a loved one with Alzheimer’s?  
Text: Families can help by being patient, keeping communication simple, and offering gentle reminders. Creating a calm routine reduces stress. Most importantly, showing love and reassurance helps the person feel safe and valued.

Title: What are the stages of Alzheimer’s?  
Text: Alzheimer’s often progresses in stages. It may begin with mild memory loss, then affect language and daily skills, and later require full-time care. The journey is different for everyone, but support at each stage brings comfort.

Title: How does Alzheimer’s affect emotions?  
Text: People with Alzheimer’s may feel anxious, confused, or frustrated when memory fails. Mood changes are common, but they are not anyone’s fault. Gentle reassurance and kindness can bring comfort in these moments.

Title: What challenges do caregivers face?  
Text: Caring for someone with Alzheimer’s can be stressful and tiring. Caregivers may feel overwhelmed or lonely. Taking breaks, asking for help, and sharing feelings with others can make caregiving more sustainable.

Title: Can Alzheimer’s be prevented?  
Text: There is no guaranteed way to prevent Alzheimer’s. However, staying active, eating healthy, managing stress, and keeping the brain engaged may support brain health. Small lifestyle steps can make a difference.

Title: Does Alzheimer’s affect sleep?  
Text: Yes, people with Alzheimer’s may have trouble sleeping or may wake up confused at night. A calm bedtime routine and a safe environment can help. Gentle reassurance during restless nights is important.

Title: How does Alzheimer’s affect communication?  
Text: Alzheimer’s can make it harder to find words or follow conversations. Speaking slowly, using simple sentences, and listening patiently can help. What matters most is the warmth behind the words.

Title: Why is nutrition important in Alzheimer’s care?  
Text: Eating balanced meals helps keep the body and mind strong. Sometimes reminders or simple foods make it easier for the person to eat well. Mealtimes can also be moments of comfort and connection.

Title: What should families know about the future with Alzheimer’s?  
Text: Alzheimer’s is a progressive condition, meaning needs increase over time. Planning ahead for care, support, and resources helps families feel more prepared. With compassion and togetherness, the journey can be faced with strength.

Title: अल्ज़ाइमर के शुरुआती लक्षण  
Text: शुरुआती लक्षणों में भूलना, समय और जगह को लेकर भ्रम, और बार-बार सवाल पूछना शामिल हो सकते हैं।

Title: अल्ज़ाइमर का जोखिम किन कारणों से बढ़ता है?  
Text: उम्र, परिवार का इतिहास और जीवनशैली से जुड़ी बीमारियाँ जोखिम बढ़ा सकती हैं।

Title: अल्ज़ाइमर का पता कैसे चलता है?  
Text: डॉक्टर याददाश्त की जाँच, बातचीत और कुछ स्कैन के जरिए निदान करते हैं।

Title: ಅಲ್ಜೈಮರ್ಸ್‌ನ ಪ್ರಾರಂಭಿಕ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು  
Text: ನೆನಪು ತಪ್ಪುವುದು, ಸಮಯ/ಸ್ಥಳದಲ್ಲಿ ಗೊಂದಲ, ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳನ್ನು ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಿಸುವುದು ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳಾಗಬಹುದು.

Title: ಅಲ್ಜೈಮರ್ಸ್ ರೋಗದ ಅಪಾಯವನ್ನು ಏನು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ?  
Text: ವಯಸ್ಸು, ಕುಟುಂಬ ಇತಿಹಾಸ ಮತ್ತು ಹೃದಯ ರೋಗಗಳಂತಹ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಗಳು ಅಪಾಯವನ್ನು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸಬಹುದು.

Title: ಅಲ್ಜೈಮರ್ಸ್ ರೋಗವನ್ನು ಹೇಗೆ ಪತ್ತೆಹಚ್ಚುತ್ತಾರೆ?  
Text: ವೈದ್ಯರು ನೆನಪು ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ, ಪ್ರಶ್ನೋತ್ತರ ಮತ್ತು ಕೆಲವು ಸ್ಕ್ಯಾನ್ ಮೂಲಕ ಪತ್ತೆಹಚ್ಚುತ್ತಾರೆ.
